text: Thirteen small plates, each doing one clear job with redstone: gates, memory, clocks and counters.
Place one on a block face; the face it points out of is its **output**. On a machine, a drum or another plate, crouch while placing, or the click works that block instead.

Right-click a plate to hear what it is doing. Crouch and right-click Heartbeat, Drift or Tally with an empty hand to change its count. A **Totem Wrench** syncs plates so they hear each other with no wire at all: see Syncing plates.
Every plate is built around [Song Thread](song_thread), which needs **Loom Thread** from the March, so plates come after your first trip there.
pages.title: Song plates
Which side is which
text: A plate's **back** is the block it is mounted on. Its front points away from that block; it powers only the block right in front, and only weakly, so it never latches through stone.

- **Unary** plates (Inverse, Echo, Drift, Strike, Chance, Tally, Verse) read the **back**. Power the block they sit on: a lever on it, dust into it, or mount the plate straight onto a Pulse Threshold. Song Thread never powers the block it touches, so to read a thread line, mount the plate on the last thread itself.
- **Binary** plates (Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush) read **left and right**, as seen from behind the plate. On a floor or ceiling, left is west and right is east.
- **Memory** reads left to set and right to clear. **Heartbeat** needs no input.
A plate hears only power pointed into it: a repeater facing away is not heard, and neither is another plate pointed straight into it. To join two plates, sync them with the wrench.

pages.title: Syncing plates
text: Plates need no wire between them. Crouch-use a plate with a **Totem Wrench** to hold its song, then use the wrench on another plate: that plate now hears the first, as if a wire ran into it.

- **Where you click picks the ear.** Click the left or right half of a Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush or Memory Plate to feed that side. Unary plates hear it on their back; on a Tally the left half is the reset. A Heartbeat hears nothing.
- **A sync runs one way.** Each plate hears up to **8** others within **32 blocks**, in the same world. The wrench keeps the song, so one source can feed a whole row.
- **Use the wrench on the pair again to unsync it.** Crouch-use the wrench in the air to let go of the song.
A new sync costs **1 Pulse** from a carried cell, or a point of the wrench.
A server can change the reach and the cap with **plateLinkRange** and **plateLinkMax**. Syncs made before a change are kept; one now out of reach is heard as 0.
A plate belongs to whoever set it down and their camp: anyone may read it, but syncing someone else's plate, holding its song or changing its count is refused.

pages.title: Reading a sync
text: Use the wrench on a plate while holding no song, or crouch and right-click it with this book, to list every plate it hears: where it is, which ear, how far, and what it is singing. Sparks trace each sync for you.

A synced plate hears its source as it stood a tick ago, so a ring of plates is safe: two Echo Plates that hear each other hold whatever they agree on, and two Inverse Plates that hear each other make a clock that flips every tick.
Break a source and its listeners forget it. A source in an unloaded chunk is heard as **0** until it loads again; a plate never loads a chunk to listen.

pages.title: Chorus, Gathering, Discord, Hush
text: Four ways two voices can agree:
- **Chorus** (AND) sings only when left and right are both live.
- **Gathering** (OR) sings when either side is live.
- **Discord** (XOR) sings when the sides disagree.
- **Hush** (NAND) sings unless both sides are live.
The answer is **15 or 0** from the facing. Put Song Thread on that face to carry it on, or sync another plate to hear it.

pages.title: Inverse and Echo
text: One voice, turned or carried.
- **Inverse** (NOT) sings while its back is quiet, and hushes when the back is live.
- **Echo** (BUFFER) copies the back: live stays live, at a full 15.
Use Inverse to turn a Pulse Threshold into a 'too empty' alarm. Use Echo to bring a fading Song Thread back to full strength.

pages.title: Memory, Tally, Verse
text: These plates remember.
- **Memory**: a live left sets it to 15; a live right clears it. The output stays until told otherwise. If both are live, clear wins.

- **Tally**: each rising edge on the back adds one. Once the count reaches the threshold it sings 15. Crouch-use with an empty hand cycles the threshold **1 to 8** (it starts at 4). A rising left resets the count.
- **Verse**: starts at **4** with no pulse. Each rising edge on the back steps it to **8**, then **12**, then **15**, then back to 4. A comparator reads the same number.
The Verse Plate is not the Verse Call: to carry redstone to a lamp or a machine with no wire, see [Verse Call and Answer](verse_link).

pages.title: Heartbeat, Drift, Strike, Chance
text: - **Heartbeat** pulses **15 for one tick**, then rests. Crouch-use cycles **20, 40, 80, 160** ticks, then back to 20; it starts at 20, one second.
- **Drift** copies the back only after it has stayed live for **4, 8, 16 or 32** ticks (crouch-use to cycle; it starts at 4), and drops as soon as the back falls.
- **Strike** gives one tick of 15 on a rising back, then goes quiet: the struck signal Drumhearts and braziers listen for.
- **Chance** flips a coin on each rising back: 15 or 0, held until the back falls.
A one-second Heartbeat on a Drumheart is a **24-Pulse** beat when the edge lands in tempo. Slower settings earn only **10** a beat.

steps.caption: An Echo Shatter we want to pause from either of two places.
Mount a Gathering Plate on the block, pointing at the station. That face is its output.
Set a lever on its left and another on its right: those are its two inputs.
Either lever on and the plate sings 15 into the station, which pauses and keeps everything it holds.
Swap in a Chorus Plate and it waits for both levers before it sings.
